title: Mental Health Chatbot — No Third-Party Data Sharing
content: A supplier of a mental health chatbot may not sell to or share with any third party a Utah user's individually identifiable health information or user input (§13-72a-201(1)). Subsection (2)'s exceptions concern individually identifiable health information: a health care provider requests it with the Utah user's consent; it is provided to the user's health plan upon the user's request; or it is shared in compliance with subsection (3). These are not a general consent exception for all user input. Under subsection (3), the supplier may share individually identifiable health information necessary for the chatbot's effective functionality with another party with which it has a contract related to that functionality. Both parties must comply with all applicable privacy and security provisions of 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and E, as if the supplier were a covered entity and the other entity a business associate. This sharing permission does not create a general permission to sell data.
